journals: One row per journal: its Mandumah code, names (printed and catalogue) and ISSN.
issues: One row per journal issue: volume, issue number and year.
articles: One row per article — the centre of everything: ids, titles, dates, pages, language, and which run built it.
article_runs: Which processing runs produced each article, and which version is the current one.
runs: One row per processing run (e.g. the first 300, the exam): model, prompt and when it was loaded.
catalogue_records: The article's record in Mandumah's MARC catalogue, as the catalogue has it.
catalogue_authors: The authors as the catalogue lists them, with their authority ids.
article_dates: Dates printed on or known for the article: received, accepted, published.
abstracts: The article's abstracts in each language — printed on the page and/or from the catalogue.
keywords: Keywords: the author's own (printed) and the catalogue's, in each language.
subjects: Subject headings and fields of study from the catalogue.
people: One row per real person, however many articles they wrote (linked to Mandumah's author records when known).
person_names: Every spelling of each person's name: as printed, as catalogued, in Latin script.
article_authors: Who wrote which article: the author's position, the name as printed there, email, and the match to a person.
affiliations: Where each author worked on each article: university, faculty, department, country, as printed.
institutions: One row per university, faculty or department, with its parent (e.g. a faculty inside a university).
institution_variants: Every spelling of each institution's name (e.g. جامعة القاهرة / جامعة القاهره / Cairo University).
blocks: The article's text, block by block (paragraph, heading, verse…), with page and place on the scan — for full-text search.
notes: Footnotes and endnotes, with their text.
note_calls: Where each note is called from in the text (the little number), linked to its note.
figures: Pictures, tables and equations: captions, descriptions in Arabic and English, words inside pictures.
works: Every work the article cites (from its reference list or footnotes), split into author, year, title, journal, pages.
work_authors: The authors of each cited work, one row each.
back_references: Citations like «المرجع السابق» / ibid. / op. cit. that point back to an earlier citation.
citation_links: The links we found: a cited work → an article in the archive or a catalogue record, with a match score.
link_checks: Links a person checked by hand, with the verdict (right / near / wrong).
link_runs: When citation linking was last run for each article.
flags: Doubtful spots the code found on each page (e.g. a note with no call, overlapping blocks), with severity.
judge_findings: What the judge model reported on each page it looked at, and what happened (fixed, retried, sent to a person).
patches: Every correction applied on top of Gemini's answer — by the judge, a retry or a person — reversible and logged.
fixes: Words where Azure misread the print and the text was corrected (Azure's reading kept).
misprints: Suspected printing mistakes: the printed word is kept, with the likely correction beside it.
metadata_changes: Corrections to metadata (title, author name, pages…): printed form, corrected form, source and reason.
catalogue_disagreements: Where the printed article and Mandumah's catalogue disagree — the list for Mandumah to review.
meta: Facts about the database itself (version, when built).
